problems.form_value: Analysis is intention-to-treat by assigned condition (p. 6).
problems.source_says: The paper's intention-to-treat refers only to AI take-up: it keeps AI-arm writers who did not request an idea. It is not an analysis of all assigned writers. Three Human-only writers who admitted using AI were dropped, and so were writers who did not complete the study after their stories had reached the evaluators (p. 7). The sentence needs that qualifier.

problems.source_says: The paper says the evaluations of writers who did not complete the writer study were dropped. Those writers had submitted a story, and a story comes only after random assignment (Fig. 1 caption, p. 2), so at least some of the 13 non-completers had been assigned. The counts agree: 600 evaluators were each shown six stories and 3519 evaluations remain, so 81 were dropped (pp. 7-8). That is more than the three excluded Human-only stories can carry, because the retained stories have 9 to 14 reviews each. The paper does not print how many of the 13 were assigned, so n_randomized = null stays correct.

summary: The PDF supports the core assignment coding: after consent and the DAT, individual writers were randomly assigned to Human-only (no mention of or access to AI) or to the option of one or up to five GPT-4 story ideas for their own story, in a preregistered between-subjects design (pp. 2, 6, 7, 8). Two statements need correction: the paper's intention-to-treat covers only AI take-up, because assigned writers were dropped (three Human-only AI users and non-completers), and p. 7 shows that some of the 13 non-completers had written stories and so had been assigned, which the form calls unknown.
